subject.title: [Bug]: Pre-compaction memory flush never runs when the reactive overflow-recovery path fires (two disconnected compaction systems)

question: Should reactive overflow recovery be required to run the existing agentic memory-flush contract before compaction, even when that extra turn can add latency and must be guarded against repeat overflow?
rationale: The reported defect is credible, but the correct behavior on an already-overflowed request affects recovery liveness, retry budget, and the meaning of the current flush dedupe state.

options.title: Unify both compaction triggers
options.body: Route proactive and reactive compaction through one guarded pre-compaction coordinator so enabled memory flushes receive identical lifecycle semantics.

options.title: Keep reactive recovery mechanical
options.body: Preserve current overflow recovery and document that the memory-flush guarantee applies only to preflight compaction.

recommendation.title: Unify both compaction triggers
recommendation.body: Route proactive and reactive compaction through one guarded pre-compaction coordinator so enabled memory flushes receive identical lifecycle semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The original memory-flush feature history is the closest available ownership signal for deciding its intended trigger contract.
